planting.note: Site in full sun on sandy, well-drained soil where its dense, low clumps can spread naturally; water regularly during establishment, then reduce to occasional deep irrigation.

directions: Site this trunkless Brazilian coastal palm in full sun on sandy, well-drained soil where its dense, low clumps of upward-arching feathery fronds can spread naturally into a broad mounded form. It is notably salt- and wind-tolerant, making it a strong choice for beachfront dunes, coastal buffers, and seaside courtyard plantings from Florida to coastal California. Water regularly during establishment, then reduce to occasional deep irrigation since it handles both sandy drought and salt spray well. Its curved, pineapple-like fruiting spikes add ornamental interest above the foliage mass.

planting.note: Plant in full sun to light shade in consistently moist, well-drained, fertile soil, ideally grouped in triple or clustered plantings; has essentially no frost tolerance so confine to the very warmest zone 10-11 landscapes.

directions: Plant this fast-growing Australian feather palm in full sun to light shade in consistently moist, well-drained, fertile soil, ideally grouped in triple or clustered plantings the way it is traditionally used in South Florida landscapes. Its smooth green crownshaft, arching fronds, and rapid growth rate make it one of the quickest ways to establish a tropical canopy effect near patios and pools. Feed regularly with a palm-specific fertilizer to prevent potassium deficiency, a common issue in fast-growing feather palms. It has essentially no frost tolerance, so it is best confined to the very warmest zone 10-11 landscapes.

planting.note: Plant in full sun in consistently moist to wet soil, since it naturally occurs in Everglades sloughs and marsh margins and tolerates poor drainage better than almost any other landscape palm.

directions: Plant this multi-trunked Florida and Caribbean native fan palm in full sun in consistently moist to wet soil, since it naturally occurs in Everglades sloughs and marsh margins and tolerates poor drainage better than almost any other landscape palm. Its slender clustered trunks topped with bright green, fan-shaped fronds create a dense screening mass ideal for pond edges, rain gardens, and wet low spots where other palms fail. It is more cold-tolerant than its tropical origin suggests, recovering readily from foliage damage in hard freezes. Thin occasional suckers if a more open, multi-stem silhouette is preferred over a dense thicket.

planting.note: Grow in full sun on lean, gritty, fast-draining soil, mimicking the rocky Eastern Cape slopes it comes from and avoiding winter soil moisture buildup.

directions: Grow this South African cycad in full sun on lean, gritty, fast-draining soil, mimicking the rocky Eastern Cape slopes it comes from and avoiding any winter soil moisture buildup. Its rigid, powder-blue leaflets held in a tight symmetrical crown make it a striking accent for xeriscape and Mediterranean-style gardens where color contrast against green foliage is wanted. It is extremely slow-growing and drought-tolerant once established, needing only occasional deep watering through the hottest months. Protect it from prolonged freezes below the upper 20s F, as it is hardier than tropical cycads but not reliably cold-hardy.

planting.note: Plant in filtered sun to light shade and rich, well-drained soil, giving it room to eventually develop a tall, palm-like trunk; keep away from prolonged frost.

directions: Plant this Mexican cycad in a site with filtered sun to light shade and rich, well-drained soil, giving it room to eventually develop the tall, palm-like trunk that makes it one of the largest cycads grown in cultivation. Its glossy, arching, bright green pinnate fronds create a bold tropical statement near entries, courtyards, or as a specimen anchoring a large bed. It grows faster than most cycads with consistent moisture and fertilization but still takes many years to develop significant trunk height. Keep it away from prolonged frost, as it is less cold-hardy than Dioon edule but well suited to protected zone 9-10 landscapes.
